newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha pledges to quit.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha pledges to quit.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha, confronted with a Socialist victory in general elections, said on Wednesday he intended to resign once a leftist government came to power.

"Definitely. There is no doubt of that. I never had the smallest doubt in that respect," Berisha told a news conference when asked repeatedly whether he intended to quit if a leftist government was formed.
Berisha said he intended to step down as soon as legal procedures allowed.

"I have some crucial duties and responsibilities that I have to fulfil," he said in English. "One thing is sure. I am interested in seeing it completed as soon as possible, but it does not depend on me. What depends on me I will try to accelerate."

Berisha had pledged during the election campaign to step down if his Democratic Party, in power since 1992, was beaten into opposition. He had already conceded defeat and partial returns from last Sunday's voting put the Socialists in the lead.

Under Albania's post-Communist laws, Berisha is elected by parliament and must submit any resignation to the assembly. The 155-seat parliament can only be convened after the completion on Sunday of run-offs in districts where no candidate won the required 50 percent in of the vote in the first round.
